name: Dropbear SSH
author: Akshay
description: On-demand SSH/SFTP server (dropbear, repackaged from notmarek/kindle-usbnetlite) over your existing WiFi — no USB networking needed. Launching opens a status app with a Start/Stop button (talks to a small loopback-only HTTP bridge on-device, no external server) showing the connect command and password while running, plus a "Keep reachable while Kindle sleeps" checkbox — defers the device's own suspend cycle (confirmed via powerd's readyToSuspend event + powerd_test -d) so the server stays reachable through sleep instead of WiFi getting suspended with it; costs more battery (WiFi/CPU stay active), the screen itself costs nothing either way. The server also correctly keeps running after closing the app (previously it didn't — confirmed and fixed via setsid). A random password is generated on install and printed in the KPM log; set your own any time by editing /mnt/us/usbnetlite/etc/ssh_password and restarting the server. Verified working on Kindle PaperWhite 4 (kernel 4.1.x), Kindle Paperwhite 5 (kernel 4.9.77), and a Kindle Paperwhite 6 (Véra jailbreak, kernel 5.15.x). Ships a second binary build for newer/older devices per upstream's own release split, selected automatically by kernel version at install time — that second build now also bundles libcrypt.so.1 for newer Kindle firmware that doesn't ship it system-wide, a known issue shared with KOReader's own SSH plugin.
